original_test_intent: Stress the selected AMD GPU remote-management firmware write path for 24 hours using the exact AGT mode and approved image, with every cycle completing cleanly and leaving the RM/GPU/platform healthy.
original_method: Pin AGT, signed compatible RM image, GPU/RM/I2C target and expected version/bank; validate backup/recovery on a dedicated SUT; repeat one vendor-approved write transaction at a time under stable power/thermal monitoring, perform required activation/readback, reconcile all cycles over 24 elapsed hours, and stop at the first flash, version, bus, reset or health anomaly.
manual_activity: RM/GPU firmware owner approves repeated-write wear exposure, exact image/target/cadence, activation and validated recovery and owns any failure disposition and verdict.
required_inputs: Signed AGT/hash and vendor flash semantics
Signed compatible RM image/hash, expected active version/bank and stable target map
Current-version backup and validated RM recovery/reflash path
Dedicated 24-hour approval, cadence/iteration/wear budget and evidence capacity
Stable power/cooling, telemetry, watchdog and OOB access
safety_requirements: Verify target and image before each write
Serialize one cycle and any required activation/readback
Never continue to fill time, clear errors or auto-retry a failed/interrupted flash
Preserve failed state and invoke only approved recovery
agent_execution_scope: After explicit approval coordinate one cycle at a time
Capture activation/readback/health and full elapsed/cycle accounting
Stop-first-error and report without DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve repeated-write plan, wear budget, image, target and activation
Authorize destructive run and recovery owner/path
Disposition failures/incomplete window and set PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic loop does not preserve tuple, image, target, activation or readback.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only vendor-confirmed exact `./agt -i2cflm:4,100,0,1,<validated-image>` sequentially; after each cycle perform approved activation and verify expected RM version and full health before continuing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exact tuple, fifteen-minute attendance and 1,440-minute elapsed window remain; cadence is governed by approved wear/activation policy.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Journal each cycle as pre-version/target, intended image, exact flash output, activation, post-version/bank and correlated bus/GPU/platform health, with stop-first-error.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines success positively rather than by missing error text and makes all repeated writes accountable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One successful RM update or a 24-hour process that silently skips/overwrites cycles cannot satisfy endurance coverage.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated identical writes consume endurance without changing version; the engineering-approved wear/cadence plan determines whether this stress is meaningful and safe.

project_override_considerations: RM firmware owner defines activation, target bank, expected version, cadence, endurance budget and whether identical-image reflash is supported.
expected_evidence: AGT/image signatures, hashes, compatibility and stable RM/GPU/I2C identity
Backup/recovery proof, approval, cadence/wear budget and stable power/thermal preflight
Every cycle's sequence, exact argv, flash output/exit/duration and image identity
Every cycle's activation, RM version/bank readback and bus/GPU/PCIe/BMC health
First-failure/recovery record, final state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master consistently specifies exact repeated RM flash for 24 hours and zero stress-log errors.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Tool/image/target/recovery and approval are provisionable prerequisites; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Preserves exact repeated RM flash while replacing negative log scanning with per-cycle activation, version, health and lossless endurance accounting.
independent_technical_reasoning: No error string is not proof of a completed flash: logs can truncate, a tool can skip an already-current image, or activation can leave an old bank active. Each write must therefore bind an image and target to explicit completion plus post-activation version and health. Because repeated writes consume flash endurance and a failed bus transaction can corrupt the controller, the loop must stop at the first anomaly and cannot be automatically retried.
